messages:
alice.cust: Hey support — running into timeouts on long generations from our Python client. I pass timeout=(5, 120) to the client but requests are failing after ~30s with httpx.ReadTimeout. Any idea which timeout I actually need to increase?
ben.support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact code you use to construct the client and the stack trace? Also which redwood python package version (pip freeze) and python version?
alice.cust: Sure. Code:```py
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'], timeout=(5, 120))
resp = c.generate(prompt, max_tokens=2000)
```Traceback:```txt
httpx.ReadTimeout: ReadTimeout('The read operation timed out')
  File "app.py", line 42, in <module>
    resp = c.generate(prompt, max_tokens=2000)
```pip freeze shows: redwood-sdk==0.4.7
python 3.11.4
httpx==0.24.1

This is happening when we try to generate ~1k tokens.
carlos.eng: Quick context: older SDK releases forwarded your timeout tuple directly to httpx, but we also had an internal per-request cap (default 30s) to stop stuck server-side ops. That internal cap ended up clobbering longer reads. In short: the tuple you pass was only setting some httpx timeouts, not the SDK's overall request cap.
ben.support: Can you try two things and report back: 1) upgrade to latest patch of the SDK (we fixed a mismatch in 0.5.x that made the behavior explicit), 2) for a quick repro set an explicit overall timeout in the new param (request_timeout) or supply an httpx.Timeout instance. Example:```py
from redwood import Client
import httpx
t = httpx.Timeout(connect=5.0, read=300.0, write=300.0)
c = Client(api_key=..., httpx_timeout=t, request_timeout=300)
```That should keep long generations from being cut at 30s. Also note if you have retries enabled each retry uses the per-attempt timeout.
dana.oncall: Also check your retry policy — default retries=3 means total wall time can exceed a single attempt timeout (and you might see multiple ReadTimeouts in logs). For long-running generations we recommend either disabling retries for that route or increasing the request_timeout.
alice.cust: Thanks — tried upgrading to redwood-sdk==0.5.2 and set request_timeout=240 and httpx_timeout like you suggested. Also disabled retries for the call by passing retry_policy={"max_retries": 0}. Re-ran and it completed. Stack trace is gone.
carlos.eng: Great to hear. For clarity:
- timeout=(connect, read) tuple behavior (v0.4) forwarded to httpx but did not touch our internal request cap (30s).
- v0.5+ exposes request_timeout (overall cap) and httpx_timeout (low-level httpx.Timeout) so you can control both.
- retries are per attempt and will re-run the full attempt timeout.
- streaming vs non-streaming: if you stream tokens back we keep the connection open and the httpx read timeout behaves differently; you may still need large read/write timeouts for streams.
ben.support: If you can't upgrade, a workaround on 0.4.x is to set REDWOOD_DISABLE_REQUEST_CAP=1 in env (it disables the 30s cap) or increase the downstream proxy idle timeout, but that’s not ideal for prod. Upgrading is the recommended path.
deploy-bot: deploy status: redwood-sdk 0.5.2 published to pypi (2026-01-21).
alice.cust: One more oddity — after upgrade we briefly saw a different exception: "TimeoutError: overall request timed out" when retries were on. That was our misconfig: we set request_timeout=120 but each retry attempted ~120s so total >120s and the client eventually raised overall timeout from the orchestration layer. We set request_timeout=240 and left retries off for heavy jobs.
dana.oncall: Thanks for the feedback — I'll add a short note to the support KB: "Python SDK timeouts: tuple vs request_timeout vs httpx_timeout + retries interaction".
alice.cust: Awesome, that would help others. :thumbsup:
